whyEn: Weight-2 chapter feeding directly into the BC practical's graded History block: Chief Complaint and History of Chief Complaint each carry a 15% major-deficiency deduction, Past Medical History/Medications/Allergies/Last Oral Intake carry 5% each, and PCP candidates face a further 9-system Functional Inquiry capped at 15% if skipped entirely — a single missed piece can sink an otherwise clean scenario. Master the six facilitation techniques, the sensitive-topic protocols, and this chapter's own OPQRST; wherever it diverges from the BC-graded OPQRRRST/LOTARP standard, follow bcAlerts.
whyZh: 权重 2 星，但直接对接实操考试里被逐项打分的『病史』板块：C/C 与 Hx C/C 各自的严重失误扣 15%，既往史/用药/过敏/末次进食各扣 5%，PCP 级别还要额外过一套九系统 Functional Inquiry（整套漏做封顶扣 15%）——漏掉任何一项，都可能让原本干净利落的一场考试直接翻车。吃透六大沟通引导技巧、敏感话题的处理方式，以及本章自己教的 OPQRST；凡是和 BC 打分标准的 OPQRRRST/LOTARP 不一致的地方，一律以 bcAlerts 为准。

sections.titleEn: Introduction & Scene Evaluation: Diagnostic Reasoning and Role
sections.titleZh: 引言与现场评估：诊断思维与角色定位

points.en: The quick 'sick or not sick' call is built from five inputs — chief complaint, respirations, pulse, mental status, and skin signs/colour — plus mechanism of injury and visible trauma for trauma patients; together they reflect respiratory, cardiovascular and neurologic performance and set stable versus unstable.
points.zh: 『病不病』的快速判断由五项拼成：主诉、呼吸、脉搏、精神状态、皮肤征象与肤色；创伤患者再加上受伤机制与可见外伤。这五（六）项合起来反映呼吸、循环、神经三大系统的运转状况，直接定下稳定还是不稳定。

points.en: Sick-versus-not-sick is a two-step call: first qualify (is the patient sick at all), then quantify (how sick). A miserable sinus infection is sick but not life-threatening; a dusky-grey patient speaking only in one- or two-word bursts is sick and life-threatening — the second question is what changes your urgency.
points.zh: 『病不病』要分两步走：先定性（到底病不病），再定量（病多重）。鼻窦炎患者难受但不致命；皮肤灰暗、只能一两个字往外蹦地说话的患者，同样是『病』，但性质完全不同——后一步的定量判断，才是决定你紧迫程度的关键。

points.en: Most initial field diagnoses come from the chief complaint and history, not from tests you don't have access to; experienced physicians often note that hospital tests more often confirm the diagnosis the history already pointed to than overturn it.
points.zh: 现场大多数初步诊断都来自主诉与病史，而不是你手头根本没有的化验或影像；不少医生的经验之谈是，医院里做的检查，多半是在证实病史早就指向的那个诊断，而不是推翻它。

points.en: Four cognitive traps distort history-taking: premature closure (locking onto one diagnosis before finishing the differential), anchoring bias (letting one early data point fix your thinking), ascertainment bias (seeing only what your prior beliefs expect — e.g. calling every respiratory patient 'flu' during an outbreak), and confirmation bias (keeping information that fits your working diagnosis while discarding what contradicts it).
points.zh: 问诊里有四个认知陷阱：过早关闭（differential 还没排查完就锁死一个诊断）、锚定偏差（被最早拿到的一条信息定住思路，后面调整不动）、预设偏差（只看见自己原本就预期看到的——比如流感季把每个呼吸道症状患者都当流感）、确认偏差（专挑支持当前诊断的信息留下，和诊断矛盾的信息被下意识忽略）。

points.en: An undifferentiated complaint like 'chest pain' should generate roughly four to five differentials covering the high-risk, can't-miss possibilities — not just the first diagnosis that comes to mind; staying open-minded, even for a frequent-flyer patient, is what a systematic history is for.
points.zh: 像『胸痛』这种未分化的主诉，通常要在脑子里列出大约 4–5 个鉴别诊断，覆盖那些『不能漏掉』的高危可能——而不是脑子里蹦出第一个诊断就锁定它。哪怕是熟面孔的常客患者，也要用同一套系统方法走一遍，保持开放。

points.en: Medical and trauma calls use history differently: for medical complaints the history largely drives the care plan, while trauma calls are driven by mechanism and the history often changes little in the moment — but the two blend, since a medical event can cause trauma (hypoglycemia leading to a fall) and a traumatic event can trigger a medical crisis (crash stress provoking an asthma attack).
points.zh: 内科与创伤呼叫用病史的方式不一样：内科主诉靠病史撑起整个救护计划；创伤呼叫则主要靠受伤机制驱动，病史当下往往改变不了处置。但两者会互相触发——低血糖能引发跌倒（内科诱发创伤），车祸的应激也能诱发哮喘发作（创伤诱发内科急症）——评估时脑子里要同时留着这两条线。

points.en: Scene evaluation for safety and stability — covering yourself, your partner, the patient and any bystanders — is the mandatory first step before any patient contact; an injured paramedic subtracts from the rescue team's capacity rather than adding to it.
points.zh: 对现场安全与稳定性的评估——覆盖自己、队友、患者与旁观者——是接触患者前雷打不动的第一步；受伤的救护员不是多一份战力，而是从救援队伍里再减掉一份人手。

points.en: Two-person crews work best when partners actively share assessment findings and the resulting care plan with each other, rather than one person silently working through it — efficiency in a resource-limited, unstable field setting depends on that hand-off happening out loud.
points.zh: 两人组的效率，靠的是把评估发现和救护计划大声说给搭档听，而不是一个人闷头做完；在资源有限、现场又不稳定的院前环境里，这种『出声同步』直接决定整个组的效率。

sections.titleEn: Content of the Patient History: Chief Complaint, HPI and Background
sections.titleZh: 病史采集的内容：主诉、现病史与背景问题

points.en: On most calls the two pieces to secure first are the patient's name and chief complaint; everything else in the history can follow in whichever order best serves patient care and practicality.
points.zh: 多数任务里，最先要拿到手的两样东西是患者姓名和主诉；其余病史内容按最有利于患者照护、也最顺手的顺序采集就行，没有硬性先后。

points.en: The opening sequence — introduce yourself and your certification level, ask the patient's name and reason for calling, then confirm date, time, location and surrounding events — doubles as a fast orientation check to person, place, time and event.
points.zh: 开场动作固定：先自我介绍并说明执业级别，问患者姓名与呼救原因，再确认日期、时间、地点与事发经过——这一套问下来，顺带就把患者对人物、地点、时间、事件的定向力测了一遍。

points.en: When first responders are already on scene, get their findings and any care already given (bleeding controlled? oxygen started?) before re-asking the patient the same questions — it saves time and spares the patient repeat-question frustration.
points.zh: 如果第一反应人员已经在场，先拿他们的发现和已做的处置（出血控制住了吗？给氧了吗？），别把同样的问题再问患者一遍——省时间，也不会让患者被重复提问搞烦。

points.en: The history of present illness opens with the most open-ended prompt available — 'What's going on today that made you call 9-1-1?' — because a truly open question cannot be answered with a yes or no.
points.zh: 现病史的开场问题要用能想到的最开放的一句——『今天发生了什么让您叫了救护车？』——因为真正开放式的问题，没法用一个『是』或『不是』打发过去。

points.en: Rule out physiologic causes — hypoxia, hypoglycemia — before assuming inappropriate behaviour is a psychiatric emergency; jumping straight to a behavioural diagnosis skips the reversible causes that kill fastest.
points.zh: 患者行为异常时，先排除低氧、低血糖这类生理性原因，再考虑精神科急症的可能——直接给患者贴『行为问题』标签，会跳过那些进展最快、也最容易被逆转的生理性原因。

points.en: With multiple complaints, decide whether they share one origin (weakness plus palpitations may both trace to a fast pulse — ask 'has this happened before?') or are unrelated (dizziness plus an ankle injury); unrelated complaints force you to pick which one is the priority.
points.zh: 患者主诉不止一个时，先判断它们是不是同一个源头（乏力＋心慌很可能都来自心率过快——可以问『以前有过这种感觉吗？』），还是互不相关（头晕＋脚踝伤）；如果确实不相关，就必须在两者之间挑出优先处理的那一个。

points.en: The current-health-status inventory (not asked in full for every patient) spans: prescription medications with dose and frequency (mix-ups can mimic a drug reaction), OTC drugs/herbs/vitamins, allergies, tobacco and alcohol use, other drug use (offer confidentiality up front), diet, complaint-relevant screening tests, immunization status, sleep pattern, exercise, household or workplace chemical hazards, child-safety measures (seat belts, car seats, locked medicines), family disease history, home situation and safety, daily routine, and treatment-relevant religious beliefs.
points.zh: 『当前健康状况』这份清单不是每个患者都要问全，但覆盖范围包括：处方药的剂量与频率（吃错了本身就可能像药物不良反应）、非处方药/草药/维生素、过敏史、烟酒、其他药物使用（先主动承诺保密）、饮食、与主诉相关的筛查检查、疫苗接种情况、睡眠模式、运动量、家中或工作场所的化学品风险、儿童安全措施（安全带、安全座椅、药物是否上锁）、家族病史、居家状况与安全、日常作息，以及可能影响治疗的宗教信仰。

points.en: Ask about accidents or injuries within roughly the past month and about operations or hospitalizations within roughly the past six months — these windows are the ones most likely to still matter to today's presentation.
points.zh: 问事故或外伤要覆盖大约过去一个月，问手术或住院史要覆盖大约过去六个月——这两个时间窗最容易和今天的病情还有关联。

points.en: If a patient flags treatment-relevant religious beliefs, pass that information along to the receiving emergency department staff.
points.zh: 如果患者提到了会影响治疗的宗教信仰，务必把这条信息带给接诊医院的急诊团队。

points.en: The history closes with a quick body-systems screen — 'Has your doctor ever told you that you have a heart, lung, or brain problem?' — followed by lower-priority items such as bowel habits.
points.zh: 病史采集收尾时快速过一遍身体系统——『医生有没有跟您说过您有心脏、肺，或者脑部方面的问题？』——再问排便习惯这类优先级较低的项目。

points.en: BC's PCP-level practical exam formalizes that closing body-systems question into a graded nine-system Functional Inquiry — General Health, CNS, Respiratory, Cardiovascular, GI/GU, Integumentary, Musculoskeletal, Endocrine, EENT — each worth up to 5% deducted for a full miss, capped at 15% off if the whole inquiry is skipped; no deduction applies if the patient simply cannot answer (unresponsive or no available history).
points.zh: BC PCP 级别实操考试，把这个收尾式的『身体系统』提问正式化成一套要打分的九系统 Functional Inquiry（功能性问诊）：一般健康、中枢神经、呼吸、心血管、消化/泌尿生殖、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、内分泌、EENT（眼耳鼻喉）。每系统整条漏问最多扣 5%，如果整套功能性问诊全部跳过，总扣分封顶 15%；但若患者本身无反应或确实无病史可问，则不扣分。

sections.titleEn: Techniques for History Taking: Setting the Stage and Judging Reliability
sections.titleZh: 问诊技巧：营造氛围、建立关系与判断信息可靠性

points.en: Most patient relationships last under about two hours, ending at hand-off — short as it is, a clean and professional appearance plus a calm, non-judgmental demeanour is what builds first-impression rapport fast enough to matter within that window.
points.zh: 多数医患关系持续不到两小时，到交接就结束——时间虽短，干净专业的仪表加上冷静、不带评判的态度，是能在这么短时间里快速建立第一印象信任的做法。

points.en: Introduce yourself, your service and your certification level, and introduce your partner too — this opening is part of establishing the professional relationship, not just courtesy.
points.zh: 自我介绍要说清楚所属机构和执业级别，也要介绍搭档——这个开场不只是礼貌，它本身就是在建立专业关系。

points.en: Interview privately whenever possible, asking non-essential people to step back — sensitive answers (like smoking habits) go inaccurate or unspoken in front of an audience, so privacy is what makes honest disclosure possible.
points.zh: 能私下问诊就私下问，请无关人员先退开——像吸烟这类敏感问题，当着旁人的面患者往往会答得不准或干脆不答，隐私空间才是换来真实信息的前提。

points.en: Confidentiality duty is grounded in the Canada Health Act and provincial health-information privacy legislation; visibly respecting a patient's confidentiality is itself a rapport-building act, not just a legal box to check.
points.zh: 保密义务的法律依据是《加拿大卫生法》与各省的健康信息隐私立法；让患者看到你在认真保护他的隐私，本身就是在建立信任，而不只是走个法律流程。

points.en: Default to formal address (Mr./Ms./Mrs.) and let the patient invite anything more casual; avoid catch-all pet names like pal, buddy or honey — they can read as demeaning and land especially badly across cultural lines.
points.zh: 称呼默认用正式的先生/女士，让患者自己提出想被怎么称呼；避免用『哥们儿』『宝贝』这类万能昵称——这类称呼容易显得轻慢，跨文化场景下更容易踩雷。

points.en: Tell the patient you'll be taking notes so they know the information matters, but don't bury your face in the clipboard — reading off a checklist kills eye contact, so stay at the patient's eye level while you write.
points.zh: 告诉患者你会做记录，让对方知道这些信息被重视，但别把脸埋进记录本——照着清单念问题最容易丢掉眼神交流，记录时也要尽量和患者保持视线齐平。

points.en: Beyond the patient, information sources include family, friends, police and bystanders, plus facility transfer paperwork on routine transfers — but every non-patient source, even official transfer records, varies in reliability, so document the source of any second-hand information in your record.
points.zh: 除了患者本人，家属、朋友、警方与旁观者都是信息来源；常规转院任务还要看转运文件。但任何非患者本人的信息来源，哪怕是机构的正式转运记录，可靠度都参差不齐——记录时务必标明这条信息的出处。

sections.titleEn: Communication Techniques: Six Facilitation Tools and OPQRST
sections.titleZh: 沟通技巧：六大引导工具与 OPQRST

points.en: Facilitation means making it easy for the patient to share delicate information: sustained, culturally-appropriate eye contact, encouraging phrases ('that's helpful,' 'anything else?', 'please go on'), and well-timed nods or 'okay' to signal you're following.
points.zh: facilitation（促进式沟通）就是让患者更容易说出敏感信息：保持符合文化习惯的眼神交流、用鼓励性短语（『这很有帮助』『还有别的吗』『请继续说』），配合恰到好处的点头或『嗯』，让患者知道你在跟着听。

points.en: Eye contact norms vary by culture — some cultures read sustained eye contact as aggression and will avoid it while still fully listening; don't mistake averted gaze for inattention.
points.zh: 眼神交流的文化差异要留意：有些文化把持续对视理解为攻击性，患者会刻意避开眼神接触，但这不代表他没在听；别把移开视线误判成心不在焉。

points.en: Repeating a patient's own key phrase back to them ('Your chest aches?') can turn two short exchanges into a full cardiac history — years of cardiology follow-up, today's pain being unlike any prior angina, two nitroglycerin doses with no relief — proving that facilitation multiplies the yield of every question you ask.
points.zh: 把患者说过的关键词原样重复回去（『您胸口发闷？』），两句简短追问就能换来一整段心脏病史——多年心脏科随访、今天的疼痛和以往心绞痛完全不一样、已经含服两次硝酸甘油都没缓解。这说明 facilitation 能让每个问题的信息产出翻倍。

points.en: Reflection repeats the patient's own word or phrase (not your paraphrase) to invite elaboration without breaking their flow or introducing leading, biased language of your own.
points.zh: reflection（反映式回应）是重复患者自己用的词或短语，不是你自己的转述——这样既不打断患者的思路，也不会带进你自己的措辞去『带节奏』。

points.en: Clarification asks for specifics when the story is vague — turning 'not feeling like myself' into 'weak, couldn't even walk the dog' — because a fuzzy chief complaint drives guesswork-based care while a clear one drives appropriate care.
points.zh: clarification（澄清）是在描述含糊时追问细节——把『就是感觉不对劲』问成『没力气，连遛狗都做不到』——含糊的主诉只能靠猜来照护，问清楚了，照护才有依据。

points.en: Clarification also means translating layperson language: 'my sugars' means diabetes, 'fell out' means a syncopal episode, 'has the fits' means a seizure history, 'water pills' means furosemide (Lasix) — expect and translate lay vocabulary rather than assuming shared terminology.
points.zh: clarification 还包括把患者的大白话翻译成医学语言：『我这血糖』＝糖尿病，『晕过去了』＝晕厥发作，『抽风』＝癫痫/惊厥史，『利尿的药』＝呋塞米（速尿）——默认患者用的是大白话，你的工作是把它翻译过来，而不是假设双方用词一致。

points.en: Empathetic response names the emotional impact out loud ('I am so sorry to hear that') — a patient without an overt medical complaint, like one grieving a family loss, may still need a mental-health referral; paramedics meet patients at the raw moment of the event more than almost any other health role, which makes empathy especially load-bearing here.
points.zh: empathetic response（共情回应）要把情绪冲击大声说出来（『听到这个我很难过』）——一个没有明显躯体主诉的患者，比如刚失去家人的哀伤者，也可能需要心理健康转介；救护员比几乎任何其他医疗角色都更常在事件发生的第一时间接触患者，这让共情在这里格外重要。

points.en: Confrontation names an inconsistency between behaviour, the scene and the patient's story; generally avoid it, but when necessary — suspected substance use, or suicidality — stay professional and nonjudgmental. Direct questions ('Are you considering suicide?' 'Have you made a plan?') are the correct way to confront suicidal ideation, not avoidance.
points.zh: confrontation（对质式沟通）是指出患者行为、现场情况与其说法之间的矛盾之处；一般能不用就不用，但在必要时（怀疑物质使用、或有自杀风险）要专业、不带评判地用上。面对自杀意念，正确做法是直接问（『你有想过自杀吗？』『有具体计划吗？』），而不是回避不问。

points.en: Interpretation infers the unspoken cause of distress and checks it with the patient — 'So, if I understand you correctly…' — when the patient won't or can't state it directly.
points.zh: interpretation（推断式回应）是在患者不愿或说不出口时，替他推断出未说明的痛苦根源，再回去核实——『那如果我理解得没错的话……』。

points.en: Never open with 'Are you okay?' — it's the easiest question in the world to answer with a flat yes or no and learn nothing. Get facts first, then loop back to feelings, and validate rather than minimize ('this is a tough situation').
points.zh: 别一上来就问『你还好吗？』——这是全世界最容易被一句『还好』打发掉、什么都问不出来的问题。先问事实，再回头问感受，并且要肯定患者的感受而不是轻描淡写（『这确实很难熬』）。

points.en: Region/quality/severity probing for a complaint like abdominal pain runs through: point-with-one-finger localization, whether it radiates or moves, sharp-versus-dull quality, constant-versus-intermittent pattern, and a 1-to-10 severity scale (10 being the worst pain ever felt).
points.zh: 以腹痛为例，展开主诉时会依次问：能不能用一根手指指出具体位置、痛感会不会放射或转移、是锐痛还是钝痛、是持续性还是阵发性，以及用 1 到 10 分打分（10 分＝这辈子最痛）。

points.en: This chapter's own chief-complaint expander is OPQRST: Onset, Provocation (what brought it on, and what worsens or relieves it), Quality, Region/Radiation/Referral (one combined R), Severity (1-10), Time (onset, duration, constant or intermittent).
points.zh: 本章教的主诉展开口诀是 OPQRST：Onset 起病、Provocation 诱因（什么引发的、什么会加重或缓解）、Quality 性质、Region/Radiation/Referral 部位/放射/牵涉（合并成一个 R）、Severity 严重度（1–10 分）、Time 时间（何时起病、持续多久、持续性还是间歇性）。

points.en: Critical thinking has five components: concept formation, data interpretation, applying principles (guidelines or algorithms), reflection-in-action (adjusting your read mid-call as new information arrives), and reflection-on-action (an honest post-call critique that turns the run into learning).
points.zh: 批判性思维包含五个环节：概念形成、资料解读、原则运用（协议或流程）、行动中反思（随新信息实时调整判断）、行动后反思（诚实复盘这一趟任务，把经验变成成长）。

points.en: Ask, then wait: one or two seconds of silence can feel like an eternity to you but is normal processing time for the patient — they may not have heard, understood, or decided yet whether to trust you. Match your vocabulary to the patient's evident health literacy, and track nonverbal cues (facial expression, sighs, finger-pointing) throughout.
points.zh: 问完就等：一两秒的沉默对你来说像过了很久，但对患者来说只是正常的反应时间——可能是没听清、没理解，或者还在判断该不该信任你。用词要匹配患者显露出的医学素养水平，全程留意非语言信号（表情、叹气、手指指点）。

points.en: Direct, closed questions still have a place — use them once open-ended questioning has run its course, to pin down a specific date, time or fact; the real skill is knowing when to widen the question and when to narrow it.
points.zh: 封闭式直接提问依然有用武之地——在开放式提问问出该问的之后，用它来钉死具体的日期、时间或事实；真正的功夫在于判断什么时候该把问题问宽，什么时候该收窄。

sections.titleEn: History on Sensitive Topics: Substance Use, Domestic Violence, Sexual History
sections.titleZh: 敏感话题问诊：物质滥用、家庭暴力与性史

points.en: People who regularly misuse alcohol or drugs get skilled at hiding it from friends, family and coworkers for years; the reflexive answer to 'how many drinks' is often 'two' regardless of actual intake — expect underreporting, not an accurate count.
points.zh: 长期酗酒或滥用药物的人，往往已经练就了对亲友同事隐瞒多年的本事；问『喝了几杯』，条件反射式的回答常常是『两杯』，不管实际喝了多少——预设患者会少报，而不是如实报。

points.en: Slightly under half of all motor-vehicle collisions involve alcohol, but just over half of FATAL motor-vehicle collisions do — severity tracks with alcohol involvement, which is one more reason an alcohol-impaired history should be treated as unreliable.
points.zh: 全部车祸中略少于一半涉及酒精，但致命车祸里涉及酒精的比例反而超过一半——车祸越严重，酒精牵涉的可能性越高，这也是酒精影响下的病史必须当作不可靠信息处理的原因之一。

points.en: If a significant trauma patient denies neck or back pain but you smell alcohol or suspect drug use, restrict spinal motion anyway — intoxication masks pain and makes the denial itself unreliable, so your own precaution should override it.
points.zh: 如果一个经历过明显创伤机制的患者否认颈背痛，但你闻到酒味或怀疑其使用药物，仍然要做脊柱活动限制——醉酒/嗑药会掩盖疼痛感，患者的否认本身就不可信，这时该以你自己的防护判断为准。

points.en: Alcohol is legal so patients may admit it more readily; illegal substance use is hidden out of fear of legal consequences — proactively promise confidentiality to improve disclosure, and never let appearance or social class bias your differential (an unkempt patient may have a head injury, not intoxication; a well-dressed patient may be the one who was drinking).
points.zh: 酒精合法，患者相对容易承认；非法物质因为怕惹上法律麻烦而更容易被隐瞒——主动承诺保密能提高患者说实话的意愿，也别让外表或社会地位影响你的判断：衣着邋遢的患者可能是头部外伤而不是喝多了，衣冠整齐的患者反而可能是真的喝了酒。

points.en: Paramedics must report suspected physical abuse or domestic violence — never accuse anyone at the scene, call police instead. Red flags include injuries inconsistent with the given story, multiple injuries at different healing stages, a partner who answers every question for the patient, and a cowering posture.
points.zh: 怀疑存在躯体虐待或家庭暴力必须报告——现场绝不能当面指控，改为请求警力介入。可疑信号包括：伤情和患者说法对不上、多处不同愈合阶段的旧伤、有人抢着替患者回答每一个问题、以及畏缩的体态。

points.en: To separate a controlling partner from the patient, send them to help at the ambulance — once the door closes, patients sometimes disclose abuse directly. If you're suddenly in danger, use a prearranged code word with your partner (e.g., asking for 'the Ferno stretcher') to silently call for police backup.
points.zh: 想把控制欲强的伴侣和患者分开，可以请对方去救护车帮忙——车门一关，患者有时会直接说出被家暴的事实。如果突然察觉自己身处险境，用和搭档事先约好的暗号（比如说『去拿一下 Ferno 担架』）就能不动声色地求援叫警察。

points.en: Never work a potential domestic-violence call without law enforcement present — these are among the most dangerous call types for both EMS and police.
points.zh: 涉及潜在家暴的任务绝不能在没有警力到场的情况下单独处理——这类任务是救护员和警方都公认最危险的一类。

points.en: Sexual history is taken in the most private setting possible: for women with acute abdominal pain, discharge, dysuria or lesions, ask about last menstrual period, last intercourse, vaginal bleeding, multiple partners, discharge characteristics and birth control; for men with dysuria, discharge or lesions, ask about the most recent sexual encounter, condom use and lesion/discharge characteristics; both sexes may need an HIV/hepatitis testing history — stay neutral, never inject opinions about the patient's choices.
points.zh: 性史要在尽量私密的环境里采集：女性有急性腹痛、分泌物、排尿痛或生殖器病灶时，问末次月经、末次性行为、阴道出血、多个性伴侣、分泌物性状与避孕方式；男性有排尿痛、分泌物或病灶时，问最近一次性行为、是否使用避孕套、分泌物/病灶性状；两性都可能需要问 HIV/肝炎检测史——全程保持中立，绝不对患者的选择发表评判。

points.en: With younger teens, avoid 'Are you sexually active?' — they may read 'active' as 'frequent' and answer based on how often, not whether they've ever had sex; be direct instead.
points.zh: 对年纪较小的青少年，避免问『你有性生活吗（sexually active）』——他们可能把『active』理解成『频繁』，按频率而不是有没有发生过来回答；应该问得更直接明确。

sections.titleEn: Special Assessment Challenges I: Silence, Talkativeness, Emotion and Risk Behaviour
sections.titleZh: 特殊评估挑战（一）：沉默、多话、情绪与危险行为

points.en: Don't rush to fill silence — the patient may be gathering thoughts, recalling distant details, or deciding whether to trust you enough to answer at all; watch nonverbal distress cues (body movement, facial expression) instead of pushing for words.
points.zh: 别急着填补沉默——患者可能在整理思路、回忆久远的细节，或者还在判断要不要信任你到愿意回答的地步；这时候该看的是非语言的痛苦信号（肢体动作、表情），而不是催着对方开口。

points.en: Overly talkative patients may just be chatty by nature, but consider clinical causes too — rebound from a fight-or-flight state, recent heavy caffeine, or a stimulant like cocaine, crack or methamphetamine. Let them run free for the first few minutes, then interrupt to clarify and summarize one specific detail rather than shutting them down.
points.zh: 话特别多的患者可能只是性格使然，但也要考虑临床原因——刚从应激状态里缓过来、刚喝了浓咖啡、或者用了可卡因/快克/冰毒这类兴奋剂。前几分钟让患者自由说，之后再打断，用『澄清』的方式针对某个具体细节做总结，而不是直接打断堵回去。

points.en: 'Linked' symptoms (fluttering heart plus dizziness) may share one cause (an elevated pulse), but especially in older patients multiple independent causes are common — a diabetic in cardiac distress may forget an insulin dose already taken and re-dose. That's why checking blood glucose on any altered-mentation patient is a fixed rule, whether or not diabetes is in the history.
points.zh: 『关联性』症状（心慌＋头晕）可能出自同一个原因（心率过快），但尤其在老年患者身上，多个独立病因同时存在也很常见——一个正处于心脏危象的糖尿病患者，可能忘了自己已经打过胰岛素而重复注射。这也是为什么『意识改变的患者一律查血糖』是条铁律，不管病史里有没有糖尿病。

points.en: Expect initial anxiety on arrival to fade shortly — if it doesn't, treat that as a red flag for early physiologic shock or something hidden (abuse, illegal drug use). Hypoxia itself is a common, frequently misread cause of anxiety, presenting as sweaty, restless and easily agitated — don't mistake it for panic.
points.zh: 刚到场时患者有些焦虑很正常，预期这种焦虑会很快平复——如果没有，就要当作早期休克或有隐情（虐待、非法药物使用）的红旗信号来看待。低氧本身就是焦虑的常见诱因，且经常被误判成惊恐发作——表现为出汗、烦躁不安、极易激动，别把这当成单纯的『慌』。

points.en: Never promise an outcome you can't guarantee — telling a metal worker with a ring-avulsion injury that 'a couple of stitches' will fix him risks a devastating surprise if amputation turns out to be needed. Inappropriate reassurance can also make patients share less, not more.
points.zh: 别许下自己保证不了的结果——跟一个手指被戒指绞伤的工人说『缝几针就好了』，万一后面真的要截指，这种落差对患者是重大打击。不恰当的安慰还会让患者反而更不愿意跟你透露信息，而不是更愿意。

points.en: Never match a patient's or family member's anger — staying calm yourself is the primary de-escalation tool. Watch for threatening gestures or escalating volume; if you can't calm things down, disengage and call law enforcement rather than telling an already-angry family the police are coming (that raises tension, it doesn't lower it). If a hostile person storms out mid-conversation, follow while de-escalating rather than let them retrieve a weapon unseen.
points.zh: 面对患者或家属的愤怒，绝不能被带着一起激动——保持自己冷静是化解局面的头号工具。留意威胁性的动作或音量升高；如果实在无法安抚，就撤离现场改叫警力，而不是当着已经很愤怒的家属说『警察马上到』——这只会让气氛更紧张，不会缓和。如果有敌意的人突然中途离场，应该跟过去一边安抚一边留意，而不是任由对方到别处取出武器再回来。

points.en: Intoxication masks pain and speeds the slide from impatience to hostility — the classic case is an intoxicated driver after a minor collision wanting to leave the scene. Stay patient, diplomatic, objective and nonjudgmental: disliking the behaviour is professional, disliking the person is not.
points.zh: 醉酒/嗑药状态会掩盖疼痛感，也会让患者更快从不耐烦滑向敌意——典型场景是轻微车祸后醉酒司机坚持要开车离开。要保持耐心、外交手腕、客观、不评判：可以不喜欢患者的行为，但不能把这种反感带到对人的态度上。

points.en: Don't demand crying to stop — a calm presence, appropriate touch (a hand on the shoulder), and a quiet 'I'm in control now' tone are what usually settles it, not commands.
points.zh: 别命令患者『别哭了』——真正能让哭泣平复下来的，是你冷静的在场、恰当的肢体接触（搭一下肩膀），以及一句平静的『现在有我在』，而不是直接下命令。

points.en: Depression red flags: sadness, hopelessness, restlessness, irritability, sleep or appetite disruption, low energy, or pain with no findable source. Situational depression follows a specific stressful event and often eases as the person copes; chronic depression is ongoing without an apparent trigger. Both carry suicide risk — you must ask about the patient's feelings and follow local behavioural-emergency protocol if self-harm intent surfaces.
points.zh: 抑郁的红旗信号：情绪低落、绝望感、烦躁不安、易怒、睡眠或食欲紊乱、精力低下，或者找不到明确病因的疼痛。情境性抑郁跟随某个具体的应激事件而来，往往会随着患者慢慢适应而缓解；慢性抑郁则持续存在、没有明显诱因。两者都有自杀风险——必须主动询问患者的感受，一旦出现自伤意图就按当地行为/精神科急症规程处理。

points.en: Attraction between clinician and patient isn't abnormal, acting on it always is. If a patient becomes seductive, state firmly that the relationship is professional, and keep a partner, police officer or family member in the room as both a witness and support for the patient.
points.zh: 临床人员和患者之间产生吸引并不反常，但付诸行动永远不合适。如果患者表现出挑逗或性暗示，要坚定明确地说明这是专业关系，并让搭档、警员或家属留在房间里，既是见证，也是给患者的支持。

points.en: A story that differs sharply from what the patient later tells the ED physician isn't necessarily lying — consider hypoxia, toxic-environment exposure, stroke or TIA, mental illness, drug-induced delirium, or an organic cause like Alzheimer's, dementia or a brain tumour before assuming deception.
points.zh: 患者在现场说的和后来跟急诊医生说的版本差很多，不一定是在撒谎——先考虑低氧、毒性环境暴露、卒中/短暂性脑缺血发作、精神疾病、药物性谵妄，或阿尔茨海默病、痴呆、脑肿瘤这类器质性原因，再去怀疑患者是不是在骗你。

sections.titleEn: Special Assessment Challenges II: Cognitive Ability, Language, Senses and Sources
sections.titleZh: 特殊评估挑战（二）：认知能力、语言、感官与信息来源

points.en: Never presume you can't get a history from a patient — assume you can get something useful from everyone and keep rephrasing until you do. Drop jargon ('unstable angina') for plain language ('chest discomfort'); watch for partial answers or omissions signalling the patient doesn't know rather than won't say; pull in family or caregivers only when the patient is severely impaired.
points.zh: 永远别预设『这个患者问不出病史来』——假设每个患者都能问出点有用的东西，问不通就换个方式再问。把『不稳定型心绞痛』这种术语换成『胸口不舒服』这种大白话；留意答非所问或漏答，这往往说明患者是真不知道而不是不想说；只有在患者严重认知障碍时，才转向家属或照护者。

points.en: Prefer a real interpreter (in person, phone or radio service) over your own broken phrases or simply talking louder, which fixes nothing. If a child is the only interpreter available, look for an older, less personally-involved interpreter if one exists; keep questions simple and avoid scaring the child. Medical jargon (ECG leads, SOB, 'stool') often doesn't translate cleanly even through a fluent interpreter.
points.zh: 优先用真正的传译（现场、电话或电台传译服务），而不是靠自己蹩脚的几句外语，或者单纯把音量提高——提高音量解决不了语言障碍。如果只有孩子能当传译，尽量找一个年纪更大、跟患者关系没那么密切的人来代替；问题要简单，别吓到孩子。医学术语（ECG导联、SOB、大便）就算通过流利的传译也经常翻不准。

points.en: For mild hearing impairment, speak slower and slightly louder. For more severe loss, let the patient wear your (cleaned) stethoscope bell while you speak into it. For patients who are deaf, face them directly for lip-reading and slow your speech; for actual medical communication, get an ASL interpreter — writing questions and answers is an acceptable fallback.
points.zh: 轻度听力障碍：语速放慢、音量稍微提高就够了。较重的听力损失：把听诊器（清洁过的）耳件给患者戴上，你对着钟形头说话。完全失聪但能读唇的患者：正面面对、放慢语速；真正涉及医疗内容的沟通，要找懂手语（ASL）的传译；实在不行，靠写字问答也是可以接受的退路。

points.en: Announce your identity and purpose immediately when approaching a blind patient. If you move a chair or furniture to make room, put it back exactly where it was — a blind patient's independence depends on a stable, predictable environment. Once in the ambulance (an unfamiliar space), narrate what's happening and where you are throughout transport.
points.zh: 接近视觉障碍或全盲患者时，第一时间报上自己的身份和来意。如果为了腾地方挪动了椅子或家具，事后一定原样放回——盲人患者的独立生活能力，靠的就是环境保持稳定可预期。上了救护车这个陌生环境后，全程要口头描述正在做什么、现在到哪了。

points.en: Environmental clues reveal medical history before the patient says a word: insulin in the home implies diabetes, an oxygen tank or nebulizer implies chronic lung disease, and the name on a prescription bottle can reveal a specialist (oncologist, psychiatrist) treating the patient.
points.zh: 家中环境本身就是病史线索，患者还没开口就能读出信息：家里有胰岛素提示糖尿病，有氧气瓶或雾化器提示慢性肺病，处方药瓶上的医生名字甚至能透露出患者正在看哪个专科（肿瘤科、精神科）。

points.en: The farther you get from the patient as the primary source, the more inaccuracy risk builds — still use family and friends when the patient can't provide history, while remembering that patient confidentiality constrains what you can disclose back to them, which complicates how you phrase your own questions to relatives.
points.zh: 信息来源离患者本人越远，出错的风险就越大——但患者确实没法自述时，家属朋友依然是要用的来源；同时要记住患者保密权限制了你能反过来告诉家属多少信息，这会让你问家属问题时的措辞变得更微妙。

sections.titleEn: Conclusion: How New History Rewrites a Diagnosis Mid-Call
sections.titleZh: 结语：新病史如何在现场改写诊断

points.en: Always ask what the patient or bystanders already did before you arrived — in one case, low blood pressure and a fast pulse looked like early anaphylactic decompensation, but the real cause was a nitroglycerin dose the patient took just before your arrival ('take it when he feels bad'); self-treatment already given can fully explain vitals that otherwise look like a worsening emergency.
points.zh: 务必问清楚你到场之前患者或旁人已经做过什么处置——某案例里血压低、心率快，看起来像过敏反应正在恶化，但真正原因是患者在你到场前刚服用了硝酸甘油（他说医生教他『不舒服就吃』）。患者自行采取的处置，完全可能就是那组看似恶化的生命体征背后的真正解释。

points.en: Epinephrine route/dose branches by risk profile in anaphylaxis: severe hypotension plus wheezing points to IV epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg of the 1:10,000 concentration; without severe hypotension or airway compromise, or in an older patient with relevant cardiac history, 0.3-0.5 mg of the 1:1,000 concentration given SC is the better-fitting choice.
points.zh: 过敏反应中肾上腺素的给药途径和浓度要按风险分层走：严重低血压＋喘鸣，选静脉注射 0.3–0.5 mg（1:10,000 浓度）；没有严重低血压或气道受累，或者是有相关心脏病史的年长患者，则皮下注射 0.3–0.5 mg（1:1,000 浓度）更合适。

points.en: First, do no harm: giving epinephrine to a young healthy patient who doesn't strictly need it is usually well tolerated, but the same drug in an older patient with known angina risks provoking a myocardial infarction via increased oxygen demand — patient history changes not just what you give, but whether you give it at all.
points.zh: 首先不能造成伤害：给一个年轻健康、其实不太需要肾上腺素的患者用药，通常能耐受；但同样的药用在有心绞痛病史的年长患者身上，会因为心肌耗氧量增加而诱发心梗——病史改变的不只是『给什么药』，还有『到底该不该给』。

points.en: In that same case, diphenhydramine 25-50 mg IV remained appropriate for the hives once epinephrine was ruled out — the same history that stopped one drug still supported giving another, following local protocol.
points.zh: 同一案例里，排除肾上腺素之后，苯海拉明 25–50 mg 静注对荨麻疹依然合适——同一份病史，一边叫停了一种药，另一边仍然支持给另一种药，具体按当地规程执行。

points.en: Even a diagnosis that felt locked in must be revisited the moment new history surfaces — the same discipline as guarding against premature closure back in the introduction's cognitive-bias list.
points.zh: 哪怕一个诊断感觉已经板上钉钉，只要出现新的病史信息，就必须重新审视——这和引言部分『过早关闭』那个认知陷阱讲的是同一件事，首尾呼应。

病史采集中的批判性思维环节数
hardNumbers.value: 5 个环节（概念形成/资料解读/原则运用/行动中反思/行动后反思）

hardNumbers.itemEn: Cognitive-bias types flagged in this chapter
hardNumbers.itemZh: 本章点名的认知偏差类型数
hardNumbers.value: 4 种（过早关闭/锚定偏差/预设偏差/确认偏差）

atScene.en: Share your assessment findings and the resulting care plan with your partner out loud — a two-person crew's efficiency depends on that hand-off happening, not staying in one person's head.
atScene.zh: 把评估发现和随之而来的救护计划大声讲给搭档听——两人组的效率，靠的就是这次『出声同步』，而不是憋在一个人脑子里。

atScene.en: Dead heroes save no one, and injured heroes just add to the casualty list — check the scene for hazards before you move in.
atScene.zh: 死掉的英雄救不了任何人，受伤的英雄只是多添一个伤员——进场前先把现场的危险查一遍。

atScene.en: Don't put ideas into the patient's head with a leading, over-detailed question ('Is the pain a dull ache behind your sternum radiating to your jaw?') — ask open, then narrow.
atScene.zh: 别用带引导性的过度细节化提问替患者『填答案』（『痛感是不是胸骨后闷痛并放射到下颌？』）——先开放式提问，再逐步收窄。

atScene.en: If you're suddenly unsafe and your partner doesn't know it, use a prearranged, innocuous code word (like the name of a piece of equipment) to signal for police backup without alerting the room.
atScene.zh: 如果你突然察觉危险而搭档还不知情，用一个事先约好、听起来毫无异样的暗号（比如某件装备的名字）不动声色地示意求援。

atScene.en: Letting a patient describe pain entirely in their own words, before you supply any medical vocabulary, gets you a more useful assessment than steering them toward your terms too early.
atScene.zh: 让患者先完全用自己的话描述疼痛，别急着塞给他医学词汇——比过早用你的术语引导他，能问出更有用的评估信息。

atScene.en: Do not chart vague impressions like 'seemed off' — pin the observation to something specific (what was said, what was seen) so the next provider can act on it.
atScene.zh: 记录时别写『感觉不太对』这种模糊印象——把观察落到具体内容上（说了什么、看到了什么），下一个接手的人才能据此行动。

atScene.en: Never assume it's impossible to get a history from a patient until you've actually tried rephrasing the question a few different ways.
atScene.zh: 在真正换几种方式重新问过之前，永远别认定『这个患者问不出病史』。

confusions.en: 'History-taking is reading down a script.' It's an adaptive clinical skill — facilitation, reflection and clarification reshape the conversation in real time, not a fixed question list.
confusions.zh: 误区：『问诊就是照着清单念下去』。它是一项要随时调整的临床技能——facilitation、reflection、clarification 会实时改变对话走向，而不是一份固定问题清单。

confusions.en: 'The physical exam always outranks the history.' A poor history misdirects the exam itself, wasting the time meant to confirm or refute it.
confusions.zh: 误区：『查体永远比病史重要』。差的病史会直接带偏查体方向，本该用来验证或推翻它的检查时间也跟着白费。

confusions.en: 'Sensitive topics are best avoided.' They still need to be addressed — professionally, privately and without judgment — because skipping them just means missing information you needed.
confusions.zh: 误区：『敏感话题能不问就不问』。该问的还是要问——用专业、私密、不带评判的方式问，跳过它只会让你缺一块本该拿到的信息。

confusions.en: 'A patient who says two drinks had two drinks.' Self-reported substance use is systematically underestimated; treat the number as a floor, not a fact.
confusions.zh: 误区：『患者说喝了两杯就是两杯』。自报的物质使用量系统性偏低，这个数字该当作下限看待，而不是事实。

confusions.en: 'An anxious, talkative or silent patient just has that personality.' Rule out physiologic causes first — hypoxia, hypoglycemia, stimulant use — before treating the behaviour as a personality trait.
confusions.zh: 误区：『焦虑/话多/沉默的患者就是这种性格』。先排除低氧、低血糖、兴奋剂使用这类生理性原因，再把行为归因成性格。

confusions.en: 'A kind reassurance never hurts.' A promise you can't keep (like guaranteeing 'a couple of stitches' will fix a ring-avulsion injury) can backfire hard and also makes patients share less afterward.
confusions.zh: 误区：『安慰几句总没坏处』。兑现不了的承诺（比如打包票说『缝几针就好』结果最后要截指）会造成严重反噬，患者事后也会更不愿意跟你说实话。

confusions.en: 'Trauma calls don't need much history because mechanism tells the story.' Medical events cause trauma (hypoglycemia causing a fall) and trauma triggers medical crises (crash stress provoking asthma) — history still matters on trauma calls, just differently.
confusions.zh: 误区：『创伤呼叫机制说明一切，病史无所谓』。内科事件能引发创伤（低血糖导致跌倒），创伤事件也能诱发内科急症（车祸应激诱发哮喘）——病史在创伤呼叫里依然重要，只是作用方式不同。

confusions.en: 'Any fluent-sounding interpreter works, including a bystanding child.' A child interpreter risks both inaccuracy and trauma to the child — look for an older, less personally-involved interpreter when one exists, and never substitute your own broken phrases or a louder voice.
confusions.zh: 误区：『随便找个能翻两句的人就行，孩子也可以』。用孩子当传译既可能翻不准，也可能对孩子本身造成心理冲击——有条件时应找年纪更大、关系没那么密切的传译，也别用自己蹩脚的外语或提高音量来凑合。

mnemonics.name: OPQRST（本章版）
mnemonics.en: Onset, Provocation, Quality, Region/Radiation/Referral (one combined R), Severity, Time — this chapter's own six-part chief-complaint expander.
mnemonics.zh: 起病、诱因、性质、部位/放射/牵涉（合并成一个 R）、严重度、时间——本章自己教的六段式主诉展开口诀，注意只有一个 R，和 BC 官方版不同（见 bcAlerts）。

mnemonics.name: 六大沟通引导技巧
mnemonics.en: Facilitation, Reflection, Clarification, Empathetic Response, Confrontation, Interpretation — the six named tools this chapter teaches for drawing out a fuller, more honest history.
mnemonics.zh: Facilitation（促进）、Reflection（反映）、Clarification（澄清）、Empathetic Response（共情回应）、Confrontation（对质）、Interpretation（推断）——本章教的六种引导患者说出更完整、更真实病史的命名工具。

mnemonics.name: 病史采集五步批判性思维
mnemonics.en: Concept formation, data interpretation, application of principles, reflection-in-action, reflection-on-action — the five-part critical-thinking cycle behind good history-taking.
mnemonics.zh: 概念形成、资料解读、原则运用、行动中反思、行动后反思——支撑高质量病史采集的五步批判性思维循环。

mnemonics.name: 病史采集四大认知偏差
mnemonics.en: Premature closure, anchoring bias, ascertainment bias, confirmation bias — the four traps to watch for while building a differential from the history.
mnemonics.zh: 过早关闭、锚定偏差、预设偏差、确认偏差——从病史里搭建鉴别诊断时要警惕的四个认知陷阱。

mnemonics.name: 俗语翻译四例
mnemonics.en: 'My sugars' = diabetes; 'fell out' = syncope; 'has the fits' = seizure history; 'water pills' = furosemide (Lasix) — sample lay-to-medical translations from this chapter's clarification technique.
mnemonics.zh: 『我这血糖』＝糖尿病；『晕过去了』＝晕厥；『抽风』＝癫痫/惊厥史；『利尿的药』＝呋塞米（速尿）——本章 clarification 技巧给出的俗语转译示例。

selfCheck.qEn: What two steps make up the 'sick vs not sick' call, and what five inputs (six for trauma) feed the first step?
selfCheck.qZh: 『病不病』判断分哪两步？第一步靠哪五项信息（创伤患者是六项）？
selfCheck.aEn: Qualify (sick or not) then quantify (how sick); built from chief complaint, respirations, pulse, mental status, skin signs/colour, plus MOI and visible trauma for trauma patients.
selfCheck.aZh: 先定性（病不病）再定量（病多重）；依据主诉、呼吸、脉搏、精神状态、皮肤征象/肤色五项，创伤患者再加受伤机制与可见外伤。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the four cognitive biases in history-taking with one example each.
selfCheck.qZh: 病史采集里的四个认知偏差各是什么？各举一个例子。
selfCheck.aEn: Premature closure (locking onto one diagnosis too early); anchoring bias (fixating on one early data point); ascertainment bias (labeling every respiratory patient 'flu' during an outbreak); confirmation bias (keeping only information that fits the working diagnosis).
selfCheck.aZh: 过早关闭（诊断没排查完就锁死）；锚定偏差（被最早的一条信息定住）；预设偏差（流感季把每个呼吸道患者都当流感）；确认偏差（只留支持当前诊断的信息）。

selfCheck.qEn: State this chapter's OPQRST breakdown, then name BC's official pain-history mnemonics and how they differ.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出本章的 OPQRST 展开，再说出 BC 官方的疼痛病史口诀名称及其与本章版本的区别。
selfCheck.aEn: OPQRST: Onset, Provocation, Quality, Region/Radiation/Referral (one R), Severity, Time. BC's official standard is OPQRRRST (Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region, Radiation, Relief, Severity, Time — three separate Rs) or LOTARP; using only partial PQRST/LOTARP is graded as a moderate deficiency.
selfCheck.aZh: OPQRST：起病、诱因、性质、部位/放射/牵涉（一个 R）、严重度、时间。BC 官方标准是 OPQRRRST（起病、诱因/缓解、性质、部位、放射、缓解方式——三个独立的 R）或 LOTARP；只用了部分 PQRST 或 LOTARP 会被判为中度失误扣分。

selfCheck.qEn: What are BC's practical-exam deduction weights for Chief Complaint and History of Chief Complaint versus the other four history items?
selfCheck.qZh: BC 实操考试里，主诉与现病史的扣分权重，和另外四项病史条目的扣分权重分别是多少？
selfCheck.aEn: C/C and Hx C/C: major 15%, moderate 5%, minor 3% each. PMHx, Medications, Allergies, LOI: major 5%, moderate 3%, minor 1% each.
selfCheck.aZh: C/C 与 Hx C/C：严重 15%、中度 5%、轻微 3%（各自独立）。既往史/用药/过敏/末次进食：严重 5%、中度 3%、轻微 1%（各自独立）。

selfCheck.qEn: List the nine systems in BC's PCP-only Functional Inquiry and the total deduction cap if the whole thing is skipped.
selfCheck.qZh: 列出 BC PCP 专属 Functional Inquiry 的九个系统，以及整套跳过时的扣分封顶是多少？
selfCheck.aEn: General Health, CNS, Respiratory, Cardiovascular, GI/GU, Integumentary, Musculoskeletal, Endocrine, EENT — each up to 5% if fully missed, capped at 15% total if the whole inquiry is skipped (no deduction if the patient can't answer).
selfCheck.aZh: 一般健康、中枢神经、呼吸、心血管、消化/泌尿生殖、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、内分泌、EENT——每项整条漏问最多扣 5%，整套跳过封顶扣 15%（患者无法作答则不扣分）。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Pain-history mnemonic: textbook OPQRST vs BC OPQRRRST/LOTARP
bcAlerts.topicZh: 疼痛病史口诀：教材 OPQRST vs BC OPQRRRST/LOTARP
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter teaches a six-part OPQRST: Onset, Provocation, Quality, Region/Radiation/Referral (one combined R), Severity, Time.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章教的是六段式 OPQRST：起病、诱因、性质、部位/放射/牵涉（合并成一个 R）、严重度、时间。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's official practical standard is the eight-part OPQRRRST (Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region, Radiation, Relief, Severity, Time — three separate Rs) or the full LOTARP (Location, Onset, Type, Aggravating, Relieving, Progression); the grading criteria explicitly list 'using only parts of the PQRST or LOTARP mnemonic' as a moderate deficiency. Use the full 8-letter OPQRRRST or full LOTARP on the practical, not this chapter's shorter version.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 官方标准是八段式 OPQRRRST（起病、诱因/缓解、性质、部位、放射、缓解方式、严重度、时间——三个独立的 R）或完整版 LOTARP（部位、起病、性质、加重因素、缓解因素、进展）；官方评分标准明确把『只用了部分 PQRST 或 LOTARP』列为中度失误扣分项。实操考试要用完整的八字母 OPQRRRST 或完整 LOTARP，不能用本章这个更短的版本。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 病史各环节的扣分权重（教材未量化）
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook only says name and chief complaint are the two most important pieces to get first; it never quantifies how each history component is scored.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材只说姓名和主诉是最先要拿到的两样东西，从未量化过每个病史环节具体怎么打分。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Official grading gives Chief Complaint and History of Chief Complaint a major deficiency of 15% each (moderate 5%, minor 3%); Past Medical History, Medications, Allergies and Last Oral Intake each carry a major deficiency of 5% (moderate 3%, minor 1%). Since a pass requires 70%, a single 15% miss on C/C or Hx C/C is a serious blow to a scenario.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 官方评分标准里，C/C 与 Hx C/C 各自的严重失误扣 15%（中度 5%、轻微 3%）；既往史、用药、过敏、末次进食各自严重失误扣 5%（中度 3%、轻微 1%）。及格线是 70%，C/C 或 Hx C/C 单项就漏掉 15%，对整场考试是相当重的打击。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Body-systems review vs PCP Functional Inquiry
bcAlerts.topicZh: 身体系统问诊 vs PCP 级 Functional Inquiry
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook treats the body-systems check as one casual closing question: 'Has your doctor ever told you that you have a heart, lung, or brain problem?'
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材把身体系统检查处理成收尾时的一句随口问：『医生有没有跟您说过您有心脏、肺，或者脑部方面的问题？』
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC formalizes this into a graded nine-system Functional Inquiry for PCP candidates only — General Health, CNS, Respiratory, Cardiovascular, GI/GU, Integumentary, Musculoskeletal, Endocrine, EENT — each worth up to 5% deducted, capped at 15% if the whole inquiry is skipped; not required at the EMR level, and no deduction if the patient cannot answer.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 把这一步正式化成一套要打分的九系统 Functional Inquiry，且仅限 PCP 级别考生——一般健康、中枢神经、呼吸、心血管、消化/泌尿生殖、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、内分泌、EENT——每项最多扣 5%，整套跳过封顶扣 15%；EMR 级别不要求，患者本身无法作答时不扣分。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Generic open history vs BC's MOI-specific critical history questions
bcAlerts.topicZh: 通用开放式病史 vs BC 按机制分类的关键病史清单
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter teaches one generic, patient-driven, open-ended history process that applies across chief complaints.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章教的是一套通用、以患者叙述为主导的开放式病史流程，套用于各种主诉。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's guidelines carry separate fixed Critical History Question checklists by mechanism — MVA, Fall, Pedestrian Struck, Shooting, Stabbing — each with its own must-ask items (impact speed, compartment intrusion, height fallen, distance thrown, etc.), already structured on this site's assessment-model page; treat them as a mechanism-specific supplement layered on top of this chapter's general technique, not a replacement for it.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 考纲对 MVA、跌落、行人被撞、枪击、刺伤等不同机制各有一套固定的『关键病史问题』清单（碰撞速度、座舱侵入、坠落高度、被抛距离等必问项），已经整理在站内『评估模型』页；把它当成叠加在本章通用技巧之上的机制专属补充，而不是替代品。

bcAlerts.topicEn: History sequence: textbook flexibility vs BC's graded sequence rule
bcAlerts.topicZh: 病史顺序：教材的灵活性 vs BC 的顺序打分规则
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook explicitly says most of the history can be gathered 'in whatever order is most conducive to good patient care and most convenient,' once life threats are handled.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材明确说，处理完生命威胁之后，大部分病史可以『按最有利于患者照护、也最顺手的顺序』采集，没有固定次序。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's grading criteria deduct when C/C or Hx C/C is obtained 'out of sequence' — for example, after vital signs — if that delay negatively affects patient care, reinforcing the fixed Secondary Survey order of History then Vital signs then Head-to-toe. Sequence flexibility only applies when getting it in a different order truly would not affect care.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 官方评分标准会在 C/C 或 Hx C/C『顺序错乱』（比如放到生命体征之后才问）且因此对患者照护造成负面影响时扣分，这也印证了 Secondary Survey 固定顺序『病史→生命体征→head-to-toe』。只有在换个顺序确实不影响照护时，顺序才可以灵活处理。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Grading Criteria p.20；另见 ch17 bcAlerts『Secondary survey composition』
